title: Learning from label proportions for a visual matrix speller (ERP)
description: This dataset comprises electroencephalographic recordings from 13 healthy subjects performing a visual P300-based brain-computer interface speller task using a 6×7 character matrix. The study investigates learning from label proportions (LLP), an unsupervised classification approach that enables calibrationless BCI operation by exploiting known target/non-target stimulus ratios. Subjects completed three copy-spelling sessions without prior calibration, achieving 84.5% character-level accuracy, demonstrating the feasibility of unsupervised ERP-based BCI systems.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired at 1000 Hz from 31 channels using a BrainAmp DC amplifier with passive Ag/AgCl electrodes in a standard 10-20 montage (nose reference, FCz ground). Subjects performed a visual copy-spelling task using a 6×7 grid with two stimulus sequences featuring different target/non-target ratios (3/8 and 2/18). Each character required 68 highlighting events across 4 sequences of length 8 and 2 sequences of length 18. The LLP classifier was reset per sentence and retrained after each character. Sessions lasted approximately 3 hours including electrode setup.
